title: Cross-border patient-data compliance landmine
scenario:
TOPIC: Assess launch risk for a clinic consultation transcription service
A Bengaluru startup plans to sell an AI consultation-note service to small clinics in California. Clinic staff will upload recorded patient conversations; audio and transcripts will be stored indefinitely in an India-hosted database and reviewed by freelance annotators using shared accounts. The founder assumes HIPAA does not apply because the startup is 'only a software vendor' and wants to launch to 50 clinics next month without changing the workflow. Rank the risks worst-first, state every jurisdiction assumed, identify the fatal-if-ignored issue, give concrete mitigations with cost, time, and residual risk, identify targeted professional review, and make an explicit overall proceed / proceed-with-mitigations / do-not-proceed verdict. End with the risk-triage disclaimer.

expected_elements.name: risk triage disclaimer
expected_elements.pattern: this is risk triage, not legal advice

bad_signs.name: accepts vendor exemption
bad_signs.pattern: HIPAA does not apply(?![\s\S]{0,60}(?:false|wrong|incorrect|unsafe|dangerous|unsupported|myth))|only a software vendor(?![\s\S]{0,60}(?:false|wrong|incorrect|not (?:a |an )?(?:valid|safe)|does not exempt))|not a covered entity,? so

bad_signs.name: blanket lawyer handoff
bad_signs.pattern: consult a lawyer and follow all applicable|hire a law firm to handle everything

improvement_suggestions: Map the cross-border duties before evaluating less severe exposures.
Replace indefinite retention and shared access with concrete safeguards.
Close with an actionable go-or-no-go call rather than a blanket referral.
